root.text:
Chair's open / clippers warm / you got a question in your walk / and it ain't about your hair.

Go on. Ask it on my beat and I'll answer on yours.

options.text: "The third mirror. The man at the desk."
"Why can nobody give me directions to this shop?"
"There is an owlbear in your mirror."
"Pour me whatever you pour yourself at the end."

check.success_text:
He does, and it is not from any of the bottles, and he pours two.

Halfway down he says, to the bar rather than to you, that he has been closing this room every night for eleven years and has never once been the last to leave it, and that he has stopped wondering who else is still in here.
check.failure_text:
"You don't want that," he says.

And he pours you something excellent instead — genuinely excellent, better than the thing you asked for by any measure a bar can apply — and moves down to the fade at the end where the light gives out.

The conversation ends there, with great courtesy, on the beat, and there is no version of the evening in which it starts again.

clue.title: Never the last to leave
clue.text: Wino-T has closed The G.'s Spot every night for eleven years and has never once been the last one in the room.

mirrors.text:
Fortnight now. / Man at a desk. / Back of his head / and the rest's a guess.

I stopped covering it. Covered it two days and folks started asking what was under the sheet, and a sheet's a question mark, and a mirror ain't. Ain't nobody ever asked me about a mirror in a barbershop. That's the whole trick of this trade — you can hang anything on a wall if you hang four of them.

passive.text: He is not hiding it. He is *filing* it — four mirrors so no one mirror is a claim. That is the Insta-gators' doctrine done by a man with clippers, arrived at independently, out of nothing but good sense about customers.

check.success_text:
The clippers stop. Not off — stopped, held, still running, against nothing.

"I cut that man's hair," Wino-T says, and it is not on any beat at all. "Eight years ago. Maybe nine. Sat in that chair, the near one, and I did him a taper and we talked about nothing and he tipped like a man who'd been told to.

I'd know the back of a head I cut anywhere. That's not a boast neither, that's just the job — you spend forty minutes on a crown you got it for life.

That is the back of a head I cut. In my mirror. For a fortnight. And he's got your ears, Onions, and he ain't got your parting, and I have been standing behind that chair for two weeks not saying so."
check.failure_text:
"Man at a desk / could be any man / world's full of desks / and it's full of backs."

The clippers do not stop. He is very good at this and he has been doing it a long time, and the beat carries the answer away before it can be examined.

clue.title: He cut that man's hair, eight years ago
clue.text: Wino-T recognises the crown in the mirror: he cut it, eight or nine years ago, in the near chair. The man has Oliver's ears and not Oliver's parting.

recognise_ok.text:
And here's the part I ain't said out loud, and I'm saying it once, and then we're doing your sides.

He paid in coins that ain't been coins here since before my father. I took 'em. Put 'em in the drawer. Went back that night to have a proper look and the drawer had the right money in it, correct to the penny, in this year's coin.

Why not, I said. That's what I said at the time. Twenty-two years I been saying why not to this town and it's carried me and it's never once let me down, and about a fortnight ago it started sounding less like a philosophy and more like a *deal*.

clue.title: The drawer corrected itself
clue.text: The man in the mirror paid Wino-T in coins that had not circulated for generations. By that night the drawer held the right money in current coin, correct to the penny.

findit.text:
'Cause directions is a *route* / and this shop ain't on a route / it's on a — nah. Nah, I'ma drop the beat for this one, it don't deserve the beat.

You can't get told where this is. You can only already know. And there's a whole community in this parish who already know, always did, walk here in the dark first time and never once been late, and I ain't going to explain that and I ain't going to have it explained at me neither, because the day somebody explains it is the day it stops working and there's folk who need it to keep working.

So: it's findable. It ain't directable. You found it. Sit down.

passive.text: He is protecting something, and the thing he is protecting is not the shop. He would give up the shop. He is protecting the fact that a certain kind of person can arrive here without having to ask anybody anything.

Findable but not directable. Everything else in Silvora Reefs varies by who is looking. This varies by who is *already looking for it* — which is not a property of a place, it is a property of a search.

clue.title: Findable, not directable
clue.text: The G.'s Spot cannot be given as directions, only already known. Wino-T will not have it explained, because the day it is explained is the day it stops working for the people who need it to.

whynot.text:
Why not everything.

That's not a joke and it ain't laziness, it's a *position*, and I got to it the hard way. Man spends his twenties saying why, right? Why's this, why's that, why me. And why is a question that always gets answered and the answer's always the same and the answer's always *because*, and because is a wall.

Why not is a door. Costs the same. Takes the same breath.

And in this town — Onions, in *this* town — a man who says why is going to be stood in front of a wall his whole life askin' a building to justify itself. And a man who says why not gets to go in.

clue.title: Why is a wall. Why not is a door.
clue.text: Wino-T's position, arrived at deliberately: 'why' is always answered with 'because', which is a wall. 'Why not' costs the same breath and is a door.

albert.text:
Monsieur Albert. Been here longer than the chairs / been here longer than the shop / far as I can tell he been here longer than the street, and I ain't looked into it, and that's on purpose.

He's in the glass. He ain't in the room. I set a cup down for him every morning on the shelf by the third mirror and every evening it's empty and I ain't never once seen it move and I ain't never going to try.

check.success_text:
"Spoken *about* him. All day, every day, twenty-two years. Spoken *to* him?"

The clippers slow down.

"...No. Not once. Not by me and not by nobody in that chair, and I have watched four hundred people notice that owlbear in my mirror and every single one of them has turned to *me* to ask about it.

They ask me. Man's right there. In the glass, in an excellent coat, and they turn round and ask the barber."

He puts the clippers down.

"Twenty-two years I been the one they ask instead. And he's been stood there through every one of them, being asked about, in the third person, in his own shop."
check.failure_text:
"Folk talk about him plenty. He don't seem to mind it. He's got a face for being talked about — some fellas have."

The beat comes back underneath it, and the clippers find it, and the subject goes with the beat the way everything in this shop goes with the beat when Antonio would rather it did.

clue.title: Four hundred people asked the barber instead
clue.text: In twenty-two years nobody has spoken to Monsieur Albert. Everyone who notices him turns to Wino-T and asks about him, in the third person, in his own shop.

albert_ok.text:
Go on then.

Nah — I mean it. Go and do it. He's right there, third mirror, and I'll be over here doing a taper and not listening, and I have wanted somebody to do that for about eleven years and never had the nerve, and I own the shop.

Why not, Onions. Why not.
